deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up the basic groupoid for Grothendieck's 1983 Teichmüller notes, which feed into the 'Teichmüller tower' of the Esquisse d'un programme.

Objects. Triples (X, Σ̃, R):
- X is a compact oriented surface with boundary.
- Σ̃ is a compact 1-dimensional submanifold of X containing ∂X. A marginal note writes Σ̃ = ∂X ⊔ Σ.
- R is a finite subset (of Σ, or more likely of Σ̃; see the corrections).
- Naming: the components of Σ are the cutting circles ('cercles de découpage'), the components of ∂X are the joining circles ('cercles de raccord'), and the points of R are rigidification vertices ('sommets de rigidification'). The components of X are the components of the object.
- A margin note says one may view R as 'rigidifying' or, for Σ̃, as 'decomposing'.

Arrows. Isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms. This gives the groupoid S_*𝔗D_top: S_* for special/rigidifying points, D for decomposition.

Variant. 𝔗^± allows orientation-reversing homeomorphisms. There is a tautological sequence S_*𝔗D_top → S_*𝔗D^±_top → [±1], the orientation character.

Full subgroupoids.
- R = ∅ and Σ = ∅ (i.e. Σ̃ = ∂X): the topological Teichmüller (mapping-class) groupoids 𝔗_top and 𝔗^±_top.
- Σ = ∅, R arbitrary: S_*𝔗_top and S_*𝔗^±_top, the Teichmüller groupoids rigidified 'with special points' (topological, oriented).
- R = ∅: 𝔗D_top and 𝔗D^±_top, surfaces with an unrigidified decomposition. Grothendieck judges this case 'not interesting I think, except for Σ = ∅ as well'.
- A margin note reads MD = 'modular' Mumford–Deligne, linking decompositions to boundary strata of the Deligne–Mumford compactification.

Next task. Determine π_0(S_*𝔗D_top), stated to be isomorphic to π_0 of the ± version, i.e. classify objects up to isomorphism. For this he introduces 'bi-weighted graphs' ('graphes bipondérés'). On the next page these are made precise as (S, A⃗, σ, o):
- σ is an involution on half-edges; its fixed points are free edges, i.e. legs.
- o is the origin map.
- There is a genus weight S → ℕ and a weight on free edges.
- The margin there adds that edges should also carry weights; these presumably count rigidification points per circle.

This is the dual graph of a pants/multicurve decomposition: a stable graph with legs, in the modern modular-graph formalism.
errors: No real mathematical error. The claimed bijection π_0(S_*𝔗D) ≅ π_0(S_*𝔗D^±) holds because the isomorphism type is determined by combinatorial data (genus-weighted graph, legs, number of R-points per circle). This data is invariant under mirror reversal, and any cyclic configuration of k points on a circle is homeomorphically unique.
Slight inconsistency: R ⊂ Σ is written, yet the subcase 'Σ = ∅, R arbitrary' (rigidified Teichmüller with special points) needs R to lie on ∂X too. So R ⊂ Σ̃ must be meant.
The page's weighting is incomplete, as Grothendieck himself notes on the next page: vertex weights are given but edge weights are still needed.

ideas.what: Groupoid of compact oriented surfaces with a multicurve decomposition (cutting circles) and finite rigidification points on the circles, morphisms = isotopy classes of homeomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid of rigidified pants/multicurve decompositions; 'Lego–Teichmüller' groupoid; extended surfaces with boundary marked points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Moore–Seiberg (1989); Bakalov–Kirillov (2000); Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000); Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984) in outline
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§ on the Teichmüller tower, in sketchy form; the detailed formal definitions here are unpublished

ideas.what: Variants allowing orientation reversal, with the exact sequence to [±1]
Identification of decompositions with Mumford–Deligne boundary strata ('MD = modulaire Mumford–Deligne')
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of M̄_{g,n} by dual graphs of stable curves
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of M̄_{g,ν} and its 'boundary at infinity')

ideas.what: Classification of π_0 of decomposed rigidified surfaces by bi-weighted graphs, defined (next page) via half-edges with involution, legs as fixed points, and genus weights
ideas.modern_name: Stable graphs / modular graphs (half-edge formalism with legs = fixed points of the involution)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kontsevich (1994), Getzler–Kapranov 'Modular operads' (1998); half-edge maps: Tutte, Cori (1970s)

missed.claim: In 1983 Grothendieck already formalizes the combinatorial types of decomposed surfaces as genus-weighted graphs with legs as fixed points of a half-edge involution, and edge weights for rigidification points. This is essentially the Getzler–Kapranov modular-graph formalism a decade early, explicitly linked to Mumford–Deligne strata. It is a priority detail rather than a new theorem.
missed.quote: Détermination du π_0(S_*𝔗D_top) ≃ π_0(S_*𝔗D^±_top). On introduit les graphes bipondérés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: it shows the stable-graph/modular-operad bookkeeping, the rigidified Lego groupoid and the DM stratification were unified in Grothendieck's unpublished 1983 Teichmüller notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The setup (decomposed rigidified surface groupoids, link to DM strata, classification by weighted graphs) is now standard. It was largely announced in the Esquisse. The modestly notable point is the early, precise half-edge/legs formalism and the rigidification by points on cutting circles, anticipating Bakalov–Kirillov and Getzler–Kapranov.
transcription_corrections: Header: the third component is a finite set R (written over a crossed-out symbol), not ℝ: 'Triples (X, Σ̃, R)'.
'X surface à bord compacte orientée' (compact oriented surface with boundary).
Likely 'R ⊂ Σ̃' (or R ⊂ Σ with later revision); the subcase line reads 'Σ = ∅ (corrected from ∂X), R quelconque'.
Naming: components of Σ = Σ̃∖∂X are the 'cercles de découpage'; components of ∂X are the 'cercles de raccord'; elements of R are the 'sommets de rigidification'.
Third subgroupoid remark reads '(Cas pas intéressant je crois, sauf pour Σ = ∅ également)'.
